hints: Focus on the strongest intermolecular force each molecule can make, especially whether it can donate a hydrogen bond.
Compare $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ with $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{SH}$ by thinking about O-H versus S-H hydrogen bonding and electronegativity.
Check the other pairs for a carboxylic acid in second place, since acids form very strong hydrogen-bonded dimers that are hard to beat.
walkthrough:
**Recall what controls boiling point**

Boiling needs enough energy to break intermolecular forces between molecules. Stronger forces mean higher boiling point.

Order to remember:
$$\text{hydrogen bonding} > \text{permanent dipole-dipole} > \text{induced dipole (London) forces}$$

**Compare alcohol versus thiol**

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ has an O-H group, so it forms strong hydrogen bonds between molecules. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{SH}$ has an S-H group.

Sulfur is larger and much less electronegative than oxygen, so S-H hydrogen bonding is very weak. Ethanol therefore has much stronger attractions and a higher boiling point.

**Check why the other first compounds are lower**

Carboxylic acids like $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ form extra strong hydrogen bonds, even as dimers, so they boil higher than esters, ethers and aldehydes. An alcohol like $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ also boils higher than an ether like $\text{CH}_3\text{OCH}_3$ which cannot donate hydrogen bonds.

Only the alcohol versus thiol pair has the first compound higher.

options.A: Correct. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ can donate and accept strong O-H hydrogen bonds, while $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{SH}$ has only very weak S-H interactions. Stronger forces in ethanol give it the higher boiling point (about 78 C versus about 35 C for the thiol).
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$ is an ester with only dipole-dipole forces, while $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ is a carboxylic acid with strong hydrogen bonding. The second compound boils higher, not the first.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{OCH}_3$ is an ether with no O-H bond so it cannot donate hydrogen bonds, while $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ can. The second compound (ethanol) has the higher boiling point.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$ is an aldehyde with dipole-dipole forces only, while $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ is a carboxylic acid with strong hydrogen-bonded dimers. The second compound boils much higher.
